subject: social
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Trace the stages of human evolution on earth
Name the sources of evidence for human evolution: fossils, bones, tools, cave paintings and utensils
Compare the four Stone Ages and the Iron Age
Trace how transport and communication have changed, from the wheel to satellites
Explain how writing, printing, the telegraph and the telephone changed life
Explain how trade and voyages helped commerce grow

topics.topic: The Constitution of India- Basic Features
covers: Explain why a constitution is needed and what it does
List the fundamental rights and duties of a citizen
Explain the basic features of India's democratic government
Describe the steps of an election and why choosing the right representative matters
Describe a citizen's responsibilities in a democracy
Use latitudes and longitudes to find places on a map or globe
Find out how time zones differ between places
Name the three major temperature zones: torrid, temperate and frigid
Tell weather from climate and name the factors that affect climate
Explain solar and lunar eclipses with diagrams
Explain what climate change is and why climates change
Locate India and its neighbouring countries on the world map
Compare the size of India with its neighbours
Relate the climate of different regions to the summer, winter and monsoon seasons
Name the main types of natural vegetation: tropical evergreen, deciduous, thorn and scrub, and montane forest
Compare vegetation and climate in different parts of India, and give reasons
Explain why natural vegetation must be conserved
Name the biotic and abiotic components of the environment
Explain how people in different regions of the world depend on each other
Explain the reasons for ozone depletion and for global warming
Describe the effects of global warming
Name natural disasters such as earthquakes, cyclones, floods, droughts, volcanic eruptions and landslides, with their precautions
Take part in mock drills and follow rules that reduce pollution
Explain what a resource is and give examples
Tell renewable and non-renewable resources apart
Name renewable resources: air, water, soil, plants, animals, solar energy and wind energy
Name non-renewable resources: coal, petroleum and minerals
Explain how resources are used in daily life
Suggest ways to save and conserve resources
Tell food crops from cash crops and name the main types of crops
Compare old and new methods of farming
Explain livestock rearing
Tell man-made things from machine-made things
Tell raw materials from finished products
Name large-scale and small-scale industries
Respect the skills of craftspeople and the hard work of farmers
